title: AI industry insiders voice alarms to NYC council as local governments take up safety concerns
source_used: Associated Press story as carried by the Times Union (https://www.timesunion.com/business/article/ai-industry-insiders-voice-alarms-to-nyc-council-22463491.php), fuller later version; GazetteXtra copy checked; Fortune's own account of the hearing used as a cross-check
key_facts: On Monday 5 Oct 2026 the New York City Council held a hearing on AI safety in Manhattan; recently departed employees of Anthropic, OpenAI and Google DeepMind described a reckless culture at the firms (AP).

Jacob Coxon, a former Anthropic engineer who AP says has become a leading voice for regulation, told the council it is more likely than not that humanity loses control to AI on the current path, and that this could end in human extinction.
Coxon said the companies run on a startup mindset of 'Move fast, break things, fix them later', which he said does not work for building the most powerful technology ever built.

A panel of staff from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta said their systems already improve people's daily lives and that they are laser-focused on safety; Anthropic's Logan Graham said the company welcomes 'smart regulation'.

Council Speaker Julie Menin asked each company to quantify the worst-case catastrophic risk; OpenAI's Morgan Dwyer said he did not know, that no level from 1% to 20% is acceptable, and Menin called the answer 'flippant at best'.
The council is considering several AI rules, including disclosure of information about AI tools, third-party approval for AI systems in the city, and letting whistleblowers receive a share of fines.

AP says the Trump administration has taken a passive approach and Congress has proven inactive, so state and city governments are weighing their own rules; New York Gov. Kathy Hochul has moved to set reporting and transparency standards.
quote_evidence: “On the current path, I think it is more likely than not that humanity loses control to these AIs and it could end in human extinction,” Coxon said.

At a hearing of the New York City Council, recently departed employees of Anthropic, OpenAI and Google DeepMind described a reckless culture at the firms, saying the biggest tech companies are racing to create technology they do not understand how to control.

A panel of AI company staffers — representing tech giants OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta — also testified at the hearing in Manhattan on Monday, telling officials that their systems are already improving people's daily lives and stressing that they are laser-focused on safety.
why_it_matters_hint: With Washington passive, the largest US city is weighing its own AI rules after hearing insiders' warnings and company replies.
event_date: Monday 5 Oct 2026 (hearing of the New York City Council)
